notes.text: The leaf is headed Proposition and is numbered 5), with a later thin 19 in the lower-left margin. It asserts an equivalence between the category of systems (X,Y,(X_i),T), explicitly restricted by the parenthesis (pour les iso), and a category of exterior/boundary data (X*, dot X, (X_i*), Y, dot X to Y). The final two assertions concern strict transversality and equisingularity. This paragraph reports the source; it is not a proof of the equivalence.

Literal source states and apparent slips are retained. The added Si T voisinage cônique strict does not visibly cancel the live Pour que T soit strictement beneath it, so the resulting prose remains syntactically unreconciled. The second-category sentence calls dot X and X_i* closed parts of X, not X*. In the later boundary condition an independent oblique upper mark gives preferred dot X* where the argument would normally call for X*. The final definition uses dot X_i = X_i intersect dot X, with no star on its right-hand X_i. None of those forms has been repaired from the intended construction.

Main-reader deduction, checked here on the specified example: under a broad compatibility convention allowing a full-ray subcone S=(A times I) union C with f(A) contained in C, exterior family data need not determine the base subset C. Let Y={a,b} be discrete, X=T=Y times [0,1], base Y times {0}, boundary dot T=Y times {1}, and X*=dot T. Compare a one-member family X_i=empty with X_i={(a,0)}. Both are closed, action-invariant subcones under that broad convention, and both have X_i*=empty. Their exterior data (X*,dot X,(X_i*),Y,f) coincide, with f the two-point identity under the evident identifications, but the first-category systems cannot be isomorphic because an isomorphism cannot carry the empty family member to a nonempty one. Thus the canonical exterior-data assignment is not an equivalence under that interpretation. A strict/full-base condition C=f(A), or an equivalent hypothesis retaining the base subsets, excludes this example. The assigned leaf does not itself specify enough definitions to decide which interpretation was intended.

Main-reader deduction, independently checked on the described graph: suppose conical neighbourhood means only a closed conical subspace that is a neighbourhood of its base, without a further ambient gluing/interior condition. Let X be the horizontal interval [0,1] with a vertical interval attached at q=3/8, let Y={0}, and let T=[0,1/2] on the horizontal interval, with dot T={1/2} and its ordinary radial interval action. T is a closed conical neighbourhood of Y. The exterior X*=X minus [0,1/2) consists of the horizontal [1/2,1] and the punctured vertical branch; the attachment point q has been removed. Those two components are disconnected in X*. Gluing T to X* only at dot T reconstructs a horizontal interval disjoint from that punctured branch, whereas the original graph X is connected. Therefore the canonical reconstruction fails under this broad neighbourhood interpretation even with no family. If the earlier definition requires the ambient gluing property or openness of the stated interior, this example is excluded; that assumption is not supplied on the present leaf. Equivalently, compare the original connected graph with the disconnected disjoint union of a full horizontal [0,1] and a punctured vertical (0,1], using the same horizontal T and base. Their exterior data are isomorphic, but their ambient spaces are not. This strengthens the diagnostic from a failed reconstruction to failure to distinguish source isomorphism classes under the same broad interpretation.

Targeted conditional check by this reader: if T and X*=X minus the designated interior are both closed in X, cover X, and intersect exactly in dot T, then their subspace topologies recover X as the pushout along dot T. Indeed a subset F of X is closed whenever F intersect T and F intersect X* are closed in those two spaces, because they are then closed in X and F is their finite union. This proves the final-topology/gluing assertion under the stated extra hypotheses. It does not resolve the independent family-information loss in N03 and is not claimed as a verification that the source hypotheses already imply these conditions.

The page records a boundary-subspace criterion for strict transversality and a simultaneous local-triviality criterion for equisingularity. The three-object diagram places (dot X_i) below dot X with an upward-open cup, and maps dot X to Y. Definitions sufficient for an independent proof of these two equivalences are not supplied on the assigned leaf, so they are carried as source assertions without a claimed proof check.

Independent audit: root personally inspected all twelve nonidentical boxes. Five box readings were revised: the first old tuple token gained f/phi alternatives, the cô opening gained local uncertainty, X_i became the preferred overworked base candidate, the live/cancelled wording gained local doubts, and the diagram arrowhead gained a headless alternative. Only the base candidate order changes the preferred lexical/symbol reading; prior first/second files remain fixed. The three-object diagram and its vertical cup were counted twice. These are visual reading decisions, not additional mathematical proof checks.
